raw_text:
Thanks — I’ll build a 12‑week, cycle-aware strength programme that begins 2026-06-01 and respects the client’s severe primary dysmenorrhea restrictions: no high‑intensity work, no heavy Valsalva lifting, and no jumping on cycle days 1–3 (i.e., flow days). Outside those days she’s fully cleared. You said her last period started 2026-05-01 and her cycle is 28 days, so I’ll use that to map cycle phases across the 12 weeks. I’ll present the plan in four 3‑week blocks (progressive stimulus with deload style weeks), with each week’s sessions written so the trainer can easily switch exercise intensity depending on whether a session falls on flow days or not.

Key assumptions and approach
- Cycle mapping: 28‑day cycle with Day 1 = 2026‑05‑01. That makes her next period start 2026‑05‑29, then 2026‑06‑26, etc. You asked to start the program 2026‑06‑01; that date falls in the follicular window after her 2026‑05‑29 menses start (so around cycle day 3 of the 2026‑05‑29 cycle). I’ll list how cycle days likely fall across calendar dates for the 12 weeks so you can schedule around actual flow days when they occur. Because cycles can vary slightly, always check with client to confirm when Day 1 actually starts; follow her reporting.
- Flow restriction rules (cycle days 1–3): absolutely no high‑intensity work, no heavy Valsalva lifting, and no jumping. I’ll provide low‑impact, lower‑load alternatives for those days (tempo control, RPE <5–6, submaximal loads, higher rep/tempo emphasis, more mobility, breathing, pelvic support strategies).
- Outside flow days: full strength progressions permitted, including heavier lifts and higher intensity.
- Programme goal: steady strength progression with periodized phases, while maintaining consistency across cycle phases. Emphasis on compound lifts, accessory work, and pelvic/core support. Include adapted sessions for flow days and guidance on nutrition and recovery across the cycle.
- RPE and load guidance: use RPE and relative percentages by week/phase. On flow days cap at RPE 5–6 and avoid heavy near‑max lifts; outside flow days use RPE up to 8–9 during peak weeks.
- Warm‑ups: each session begins with 8–12 min general warm‑up + movement prep; on flow days include diaphragmatic breathing and pelvic floor awareness.
- Progression: 3×4‑week mesocycles (Strength foundation → Build → Peak-ish) but I break into four 3‑week blocks with a lighter week every 3rd week to manage fatigue and accommodate cycle disruption. You can shift the light/recovery weeks to align with anticipated flow when needed.

Calendar mapping (quick reference)
- Last period: 2026‑05‑01 (Day 1)
- Next expected periods: 2026‑05‑29 (Day 1), 2026‑06‑26, 2026‑07‑24, 2026‑08‑21
- Program start: 2026‑06‑01 → falls in cycle that started 2026‑05‑29 (this makes 2026‑06‑01 cycle day 3 — last flow day that is restricted). From that point on, subsequent menses windows (flow days 1–3) will be approximately:
  - 2026‑06‑26 to 2026‑06‑28
  - 2026‑07‑24 to 2026‑07‑26
  - 2026‑08‑21 to 2026‑08‑23
- Always verify with client on Day 1 each month — if the period shifts a day or two, adapt the session that week to follow the flow restrictions.

Program overview
- Frequency: 3 full‑body strength sessions / week + 1 optional low‑impact conditioning/mobility session. Sessions are ~45–70 min depending on load and accessory volume.
- Session structure: A = Heavy lower-focus, B = Upper-focus/hinge emphasis, C = Squat/press with accessory and posterior chain. On flow days every session is replaced by the “Flow Day Version” (lower intensity, no Valsalva/heavy loads/no jumps).
- Equipment assumed: barbell, squat rack, bench, dumbbells, kettlebell, cable or band station, access to rowing/ergometer or bike for conditioning. If some equipment is missing, I’ll note substitutions.
- Nutrition and recovery guidance included at the end, with cycle‑specific recommendations.

Progression and intensity templates (how to read sets/reps)
- Non‑flow (standard) days: load prescribed by RPE or percentage where noted. Increase load when prescribed RPE is 1–2 below target for two consecutive sessions. Typical rep ranges:
  - Strength: 3–6 reps at RPE 7–9
  - Hypertrophy/volume: 8–12 reps at RPE 7–8
  - Conditioning: moderately intense intervals, e.g., 6–10/15–20 min efforts
- Flow days (cycle day 1–3): cap intensity. Keep RPE ≤5–6, no heavy triples/singles, no Valsalva (use lighter loads and exhale on exertion), no jumping. Focus on tempo, blood flow, mobility, and pain‑reducing strategies.

Weeks 1–3 (2026‑06‑01 to 2026‑06‑21) — Foundation phase (establish technique, baseline loads)
Structure: 3 sessions weekly (e.g., Mon/Wed/Fri). Week 3 is lighter to aid adaptation.

Week 1 (2026‑06‑01 start)
- Note: 2026‑06‑01 is cycle day ~3 (last flow day). If she’s still on flow Day 1–3 that day, use Flow Day Versions for any session in that window.

Session A — Lower strength focus
- Warm‑up: 8–10 min bike/light row; diaphragmatic breathing; hip mobility.
- Main: Back squat 4×5 @ RPE 7 (use 70–75% 1RM approximate). If this is a flow day → Goblet squats 3×10 at light load, tempo 3s down/1s up, no Valsalva.
- Accessory: Romanian deadlift 3×6–8 @ RPE 7 (flow day → kettlebell RDL 3×10, lighter load, slow tempo).
- Accessory: Split squat 3×8 each leg (bodyweight or light DBs). Flow day keep bodyweight or light DBs and pause if pelvic pressure increases.
- Core/anti‑extension: deadbug 3×12 (flow) or plank 3×30–45s (non‑flow).

Session B — Upper/hinge focus
- Warm‑up: band pull aparts, scapular work, breathing.
- Main: Romanian deadlift or trap bar deadlift 4×5 @ RPE 7–8 (if leftover flow day restrict to 3×8 kettlebell swings light, no ballistic jumping).
- Press: Bench press 4×6 @ RPE 7 (flow day → floor press or standing DB press 3×10 at RPE ≤6).
- Accessory: Bent‑over row 3×8 (flow day → seated cable/ band row 3×12).
- Core: Pallof press 3×10/side.

Session C — Squat/press accessory
- Warm‑up: dynamic hip/shoulder prep.
- Main: Front squat or goblet squat 3×6–8 @ RPE 7 (flow day → goblet squat 3×12 tempo).
- Press: Overhead press 3×6–8 (flow day → landmine press or DB press 3×10).
- Posterior chain: Glute bridge or single‑leg hip thrust 3×8–10 (flow day → banded glute activation and Lying hip thrust 3×12).
- Conditioning (optional): 12–15 min easy bike/row at conversational pace. On flow days keep it gentle.

Week 2
- Increase load modestly on main lifts if RPE allowed (add 2.5–5 kg where possible). Keep same structure.
- Introduce short technique cues for breathing: exhale on exertion, avoid breath‑holding.

Week 3 (Recovery week)
- Reduce main lift volume by ~30–40% (e.g., 3×4 with lighter loads) or substitute lighter variations.
- Focus on mobility, tempo, and technique.
- Flow days: emphasis on restorative sessions, yoga, pelvic diaphragm work.

Weeks 4–6 (2026‑06‑22 to 2026‑07‑12) — Build phase (increase intensity and specificity)
- Progress to heavier sets with slightly lower reps for primary lifts; add a dedicated heavy day if client tolerates.
- Continue 3 weekly sessions; week 6 is a lighter week.

Week 4
Session A — Heavy lower day
- Main: Back squat 5×5 @ RPE 7–8 (progress from Week 1 loads). Flow day → pause squats / goblet high‑rep variant 3×12, tempo 3s eccentric.
- Accessory: RDL 4×6.
- Accessory: Walking lunges 3×10/leg.
- Core: Plank 3×30–60s or deadbug variations on flow days.

Session B — Upper heavy/volume
- Main: Bench press 5×5 @ RPE 7–8 (flow day → DB incline 3×12).
- Pull: Weighted chin‑up or assisted pull‑up 4×5–8 (flow day → banded rows 3×12).
- Accessory: Face pulls, band pull aparts 3×15.

Session C — Dynamic/conditioning + posterior chain
- Main: Romanian deadlift or trap bar 4×4–6 heavy (flow day → kettlebell RDL 3×12).
- Secondary: Front squat 3×8 (flow → 3×12 goblet).
- Conditioning: 10–12 min EMOM of low‑impact work (row, bike) — on flow days keep to 6–8 min easy.

Week 5
- Progressive overload on main lifts (small increases). Maintain accessory volumes.

Week 6 (lighter)
- Reduce load and volume 30–40%. Replace one session with mobility/technique session.
- Flow days: restorative work (foam rolling, mobility, pelvic breathing).

Weeks 7–9 (2026‑07‑13 to 2026‑08‑02) — Intensification / strength peak
- Shift heavier on compound lifts, lower reps (3–5) and introduce singles/doubles in Week 9 if not on flow days.
- Keep in mind flow days (approx 2026‑07‑24–26 falls in Week 9 or 10 depending on mapping; adapt).

Week 7
Session A — Heavy squat focus
- Back squat 5×3 @ RPE 8 (flow day → box squats or goblet 3×10 tempo).
- Accessory: Good mornings or RDL 3×6.
- Single‑leg work 3×8.

Session B — Heavy hinge + upper
- Deadlift 5×3 @ RPE 7–8 (flow day → trap bar light 3×8 or kettlebell RDLs).
- Bench 4×4 @ RPE 8 (flow → DB press 3×12).
- Rows 3×8–10.

Session C — Press/squat mix + conditioning
- Front squat 4×4; Overhead press 4×4.
- Accessories: face pulls, band work.
- Conditioning: 12–15 min steady moderate bike (non‑flow) or 10 min gentle on flow days.

Week 8
- Add small load increases. Focus on bar speed and controlled breathing.

Week 9 (lighter/intensity modulation)
- Drop volume and intensities ~30%. If client’s period falls in this week (approx 2026‑07‑24–26 per calendar mapping), ensure restricted sessions are flow‑versions.

Weeks 10–12 (2026‑08‑03 to 2026‑08‑23) — Consolidation and sustainable peak
- Aim to consolidate strength gains; reintroduce moderate heavy triples/doubles in Week 11, then a controlled taper in Week 12. Week 12 coincides with approximate period start 2026‑08‑21 — ensure flow day adaptations.

Week 10
Session A — Squat strength 4×3–5
- Main: 4×3–5 back squat @ RPE 8 (flow day alternative as above).
- Supplemental: RDL 3×6–8, step‑ups 3×8.
- Core: anti‑extension and breathing.

Session B — Deadlift/upper
- Deadlift 4×3–5 @ RPE 8 (flow → trap bar RDLs 3×10).
- Bench 4×3–6 @ RPE 8 (flow → 3×10 DB press).
- Rows 3×8–10.

Session C — Mixed
- Pick two compound lifts at moderate intensity 3×5 each.
- Conditioning: 8–12 min moderate intervals on non‑flow days; flow days 10–20 min mobility + breathwork.

Week 11
- Slight increase in load if RPE allows, testing a tougher triple/double on a non‑flow day only.

Week 12 (taper/recovery)
- Reduce volume by ~40%, focus on technique, mobility, and recovery. If flow days fall here (approx 2026‑08‑21–23), treat them as restorative sessions.

Flow day session templates (always use these on cycle days 1–3)
- General principles: RPE ≤5–6, avoid breath‑holding. Use diaphragmatic breath and exhale on exertion, keep loads light, avoid ballistic moves, avoid maximal lifts and jumps.
- Example Flow Day Session (30–45 min):
  - Warm‑up: 8 min easy bike or walk + diaphragmatic breathing 2–3 min.
  - Movement prep: hip circles, cat/cow, glute bridges 2×15 slow.
  - Strength/tempo: Goblet squat 3×10 tempo 3s down / 1s up (light DB).
  - Hinge: Kettlebell Romanian deadlift 3×12, light load, slow.
  - Upper: Seated DB press 3×12 or banded push 3×15.
  - Core: Deadbug variations 3×12.
  - Finish: 8–12 min mobility and pelvic floor breathing work; guided relaxation if available.

Pelvic floor and breathing cues (for all sessions, emphasise on flow days)
- Encourage diaphragmatic breathing: inhale diaphragmatically (belly expands), exhale on exertion. Avoid forceful bearing down.
- Cue pelvic floor to lift gently on exertion (avoid Valsalva). Use lighter loads and higher reps if pelvic pressure increases.
- If client reports increased pelvic pressure/pain, reduce load/volume and increase rest; consider swapping to more mobility/toning work that day.

Nutrition and recovery guidance (cycle‑aware)
- Calories & protein: Aim for a slight calorie surplus if primary goal is strength/hypertrophy, or maintenance if weight stable. Protein 1.6–2.2 g/kg/day (e.g., for 60–70 kg client, ~96–154 g/day).
- On flow days: prioritize anti‑inflammatory foods and hydration. Small, frequent meals can help if nausea occurs. Increase omega‑3 rich foods (fatty fish, walnuts) and antioxidant‑rich fruits/veggies. Avoid excessive caffeine if it worsens cramps; however moderate caffeine can reduce perceived pain for some — individualize.
- Iron and B vitamins: ensure adequate iron status (especially with heavy flow). Recommend GP check ferritin if symptomatic. Include lean red meat, legumes, leafy greens, or supplementation as per GP advice.
- Electrolytes and hydration: maintain hydration across cycle; flow days may benefit from slightly increased electrolytes if cramping worsens.
- Supplements to consider (discuss with GP): low‑dose magnesium (can reduce cramping for some), omega‑3 fish oil, vitamin D if deficient; never start high‑dose supplementation without medical sign‑off.
- Recovery: prioritize sleep (7–9 h), active recovery on flow days, and heat packs/steam for pelvic cramping. Use transcutaneous electrical nerve stimulation (TENS) or analgesics per GP guidance if needed during severe pain.

Auto‑regulation and client check-ins
- Each session start: ask about pain level, pelvic pressure, fatigue. If on cycle Day 1–3 or if pain > moderate, switch to Flow Day template.
- If client reports no pain and feels good but it’s still cycle Day 1–3, still adhere to restrictions you set (no heavy lifting). For light symptoms outside that window she’s cleared for full lifting.
- Progression rule: increase loads when target RPE is undershot for 2 consecutive sessions. Regress (reduce load or reps) if RPE higher than target or pelvic symptoms arise.

Example 12‑week microcycle summary (quick view)
- Weeks 1–3: Technique & volume base; Week 3 lighter
- Weeks 4–6: Build intensity; Week 6 lighter
- Weeks 7–9: Strength intensify; Week 9 lighter
- Weeks 10–12: Consolidate & taper with Week 12 lighter
- Flow days: always use low intensity Flow Day template — these fall approximately end of June, late July, late Aug per calendar mapping but confirm each month.

Final notes for you as trainer
- Keep calendars flexible: follow client’s reported Day 1 each month and switch sessions accordingly. If heavy day lands on flow days, swap or move heavy to earlier/later non‑flow day that week.
- Track objective metrics: RPE, sets/reps completed, pelvic symptom score (0–10) each session. Use those to inform load adjustments and to notice if dysmenorrhea is improving/worsening.
- Communication: ask client to report any new or worsening symptoms to GP; continue clearance checks if any change.
- If you want, I can produce:
  - A printable 12‑week week‑by‑week table with specific loads as % of 1RM based on current lift numbers.
  - A sample 7‑day calendar for Weeks 1, 5, and 9 showing which session to move if period days overlap.
  - Pelvic floor friendly exercise cue sheet and breathing script for flow days.

Would you like me to convert this into a day‑by‑day printable program with percentages for main lifts (if you provide current 1RMs), or a calendar that shifts sessions when her menses starts on a different day?
